info.title: Rahdar API
info.description: Cluster-wide management and observability for Apache ActiveMQ Artemis

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to retry. Within 24 hours a repeat by the same user with the same method, path, query and body returns the first result with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and applies nothing again. The same key with another request is 422 `idempotency-key-reused`; while the first is still running it is 409 `idempotency-in-progress`. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; not accepted on multipart uploads. Server errors and 401, 403 and 429 are not recorded, so the retry runs.

mcpTools.description: MCP tools the token may call; empty or absent means every tool

version.description: The version of the request as shown.

paramsHash.description: Echo it, with version, to decide.

tokenName.description: The name of the API token the requester used; null for a session.

link.description: The request's page in the console.

decideRefusal.description: Why the current user may not decide it.

mfaVerified.description: Whether the current user's session verified a second factor; a policy may need it.

requesterLacksPermission.description: Whether the requester could no longer run it; null when unknown or ended.

type.description: The operation type, such as subscription.purge.

clusterId.description: The cluster's own id as the brokers report it.

managementUrlPattern.description: Artemis only: the pattern the check derived management URLs from.

contributions.description: What each enabled feature adds to the check, keyed by feature id and read from a reachable node. Empty where a system has none.

cause.description: DNS, REFUSED, TIMEOUT, TLS, AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORIZATION or UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.

address.description: The address the node advertises; null when it was never learned.

cause.description: DNS, REFUSED, TIMEOUT, TLS or AUTHENTICATION when unreachable.

support.description: Where the release sits against the supported range.

mode.description: The cluster's metadata mode, such as KRaft or ZooKeeper.

versionGates.description: Operations that need a newer Artemis release than some node runs

findings.description: Every capability the system's driver assessed for the account, with its own reason. Empty for a system whose capabilities are the fixed ones above.

seedUrls.description: The management URLs the operator gave as seeds, from the nodes that hold one

coreUsername.description: The Core account's user name, or null while Core uses the management account

credentialRejections.description: The accounts a broker rejected, and on which nodes, so the view can link to where the account is edited

username.description: The account's user name; null for a token or no account.

secretStored.description: Whether a password or token is stored.

singular.description: The name of one, such as Queue.

plural.description: The name of several, such as Queues.

id.description: The kind's id, such as artemis.queue.

resourceClass.description: The role the kind plays: SUBSCRIPTION, DESTINATION, ROUTE, CONSUMER and so on.

label.description: The kind's name for people, singular and plural.

partitioned.description: Whether the kind reads a partitioned log: browsing is by partition and offset or time.

verbs.description: What the system can do to this kind (create, delete, pause, purge, ...), plus what Rahdar adds when the system provides it (reset-counters, expire).

versionSupport.description: Where version sits against the supported Artemis range

urlSource.description: Where the management URL came from; null while there is none

urlProblem.description: Why the node has no management URL

coreUrlManual.description: Whether an operator set the Core URL

id.description: The system's id, such as artemis.

kind.description: The subscription's kind, such as artemis.queue.

destination.description: The id of the destination this subscription binds to.

attributes.description: The system's properties of the subscription: routingType (ANYCAST or MULTICAST), durable (default true), autoCreateAddress (default true), filter, maxConsumers, purgeOnNoConsumers, exclusive, nonDestructive, ringSize.

dryRun.description: Whether this was a preview that mutated nothing.

cap.description: The bulk safety cap in force.

overCap.description: Whether the summed estimate exceeds the cap.

partial.description: Whether some nodes applied the command and others did not.

totalAffected.description: Total messages destroyed, or that would be.

status.description: WOULD_APPLY on a preview; APPLIED when the node was changed; ALREADY when it was already in the requested state; SKIPPED_NOT_LIVE when the node was not live and never received the command; UNSUPPORTED_VERSION when its Artemis release lacks the operation and it was not called; FAILED when it refused.

affected.description: Messages destroyed, or that would be destroyed, on this node.

error.description: Why this node failed; otherwise what the preview warned about this node, which a real run repeats on its result.

VerifyRequest.description: Which indexed row to look for on the live broker.

VerifyView.description: Whether an indexed row is still on the broker.

presence.description: PRESENT, GONE or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is not GONE: a read that could not settle the question is never reported as an absence.

SqlExecuteRequest.description: A query to execute, and whether to keep tailing after the first pass.

SqlQueryTicketView.description: A short-lived, single-use reference to a query. The stream is opened by this reference so the query text never appears in a URL.

SqlQueryRequest.description: A query to plan or run.

NoticeView.description: Something true about a plan or result that changes how it should be read.

PlanView.description: What a query will do, worked out without contacting a broker.

source.description: BROKER or INDEX — which backend will answer.

targets.description: The queue-and-node pairs the query will read.

selector.description: The JMS selector the broker will evaluate, if any.

requiresScan.description: Whether any predicate forces messages to be read and examined.

pushedDown.description: The predicates the broker evaluates. These cost nothing.

scanned.description: The predicates Rahdar evaluates. These cost a scan.

estimatedMessagesExamined.description: How many messages the query is expected to examine.

effectiveLimit.description: The row limit that will actually apply, after the server cap.

captured.description: True when every target of this query is captured on the node it is read from, which is what lets the console claim the result is everything the address routed rather than everything a poll happened to see.

notices.description: Everything true about this plan the operator has to be told.

destination.description: The id of the destination the subscription is bound to.

mode.description: SAMPLE polls the queue and records what it saw; CAPTURE installs a divert-fed tap on every live node and records everything the address routed. CAPTURE mutates broker routing and needs capture:write.

ringSize.description: Messages the capture queue holds before the broker drops the oldest.

filterString.description: An Artemis filter applied by the divert, narrowing both load and exposure.

maxBytes.description: Payload bytes this subscription may hold before it degrades.

maxRate.description: Messages per second this subscription may ingest.

bodyCapBytes.description: Bytes of body stored per message; a longer body is stored truncated.

CaptureNodeView.description: What capture is doing on one node. Per node, because a tap is a node-local object.

detail.description: Why it is in that state, in the words to show the operator.

capturedFrom.description: When this node started being captured. Null when it never has been.

IndexSubscriptionView.description: One index subscription and what it currently holds.

messagesHeld.description: How many messages this subscription is currently holding.

bytesHeld.description: Approximate bytes of message payload held.

oldestObservedAt.description: The oldest observation still held, or null when nothing is held.

notCapturing.description: Why this subscription is recording nothing, or null when it is running. An empty index and a subscription whose pattern matches no queue look identical from a query, so the reason is stated here.

backlogInProgress.description: True while a sampled subscription is still indexing the messages that were already on its queues when it started. That walk is spread over several polls to bound broker load, and until it finishes the index is not up to date.

mode.description: SAMPLE or CAPTURE. A sampled subscription records what a poll saw; a captured one records what the address routed.

nodes.description: Capture state per node. Empty for a sampled subscription. A node missing from this list is one capture has not reached, which is not the same as one that is capturing nothing.

destinations.description: The ids of the destinations the pattern resolves to. Rahdar's own capture destinations are never included.

nodes.description: The live nodes the tap would be installed on.

ringMessages.description: Messages each capture queue holds before the broker drops the oldest.

ringBytes.description: Bytes each capture queue holds before the broker drops the oldest.

brokerObjects.description: The broker objects created on every listed node.

brokerXml.description: The equivalent permanent broker.xml for a configuration-managed estate.

refusal.description: Why capture would be refused as things stand, or null when it would not.

notes.description: Where a deny rule wins, and what is not evaluated.
